Done. Reflection summary:

What this question exposed: My regression methodology, the FFO-1 data extraction (25 chained values 1989-2013), and the cubic prediction (-2,785,303) were all **correct**. The single error was the external comparison constant — I plugged in FY2025 deficit = -1,775,587 when the correct final figure is **-1,877,649** (~$1.88T). Back-solving from the gold answer (907,654) confirms it: |−2,785,303 − (−1,877,649)| = 907,654.

The generalizable lesson — and the most dangerous part — is that my previously-saved skill had **baked the wrong constant into a worked example**, which would have propagated the same wrong answer to every future run. So this wasn't just a one-off correction; it was fixing a self-replicating error in the skill.

What I saved:
- Corrected the constant (-1,877,649) in both the SKILL.md pointer and references/multi-bulletin-timeseries-regression.md.
- Added a CRITICAL warning that for these multi-bulletin regression questions the regression is usually right and the answer hinges entirely on the external comparison constant (the #1 failure mode), plus a directive to look it up via web/search when available rather than trusting a remembered number.
- Added a sign/magnitude sanity check (diff should land ~900k, not ~1.0M).
- Compact memory pointer (within char budget).

This was genuinely generalizable and a stale-data trap, so the updates were warranted.
